# local 0001: Pointers to int that are initialized with wide string literals get bytes of a host address

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Fix together with bug #3973, which has the same cause in printIvalPtr.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For the file below, the compiler writes three literal bytes as the initial value of the pointer,
where the address of the string belongs. The file was compiled on r17176 with
`sdcc -mmcs51 --model-large wide.c`.

```c
#pragma disable_warning 244

__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[2];

int const *wide = L"AB";

void main (void)
{
  res[0] = *wide;               /* 0x41 expected */
  res[1] = 0x55;                /* main ran to its end */
}
```

```
__xinit__wide:
; generic printIvalPtr
	.byte #0x30,#0x6e,#0x62
```

`wchar_t` is `unsigned long` in SDCC, so the type of the pointer and the type of the literal
differ. The pragma disables warning 244, which the compiler prints for that difference. The bytes
change from one run of the compiler to the next. In ucsim, `res[0]` was `89` after one compile and
`ff` after another. With `--model-large --stack-auto` the compiler also writes literal bytes, and
`res[0]` was `63`. With `--model-huge` it was `bd`, in a copy of the file that also defines the
SFR `PSBANK` for the library of that model. The string itself is emitted in each case.

With `--model-small` and `--model-medium` the compiler initializes the pointer by code that loads
the address of the string, and `res[0]` is `41`. A pointer that is `const` itself,
`int const * const p = L"AB";`, gets literal bytes with the small model too.

`support/regression/tests/p99-conformance.c` defines two such objects, which get literal bytes
with the same three sets of options when they are compiled as a file of their own.

## Cause

`printIvalPtr` in `src/SDCCglue.c` calls `printIvalCharPtr`, which prints the label of the string,
only when the pointer in the declaration points to a character type or to an unsigned `int` type
of any length. `int const *` is neither. The value that `constExprValue` returns for a string
literal has the storage class `S_LITERAL`, and the numeric members of its union overlap the
compiler's pointer to the characters. `printIvalPtr` therefore executes its `IS_LITERAL` branch,
which prints the low bytes of that pointer with `aopLiteral`.

This was read from the source of r17176 and checked there in two ways. Under gdb, the value that
`printIvalPtr` printed had the storage class `S_LITERAL` and the `v_char` member
`0x56091d912c50`, and the compiler wrote `50 2c 91`. With the large model, pointers to `long` and
to `void` get literal bytes, and pointers to `unsigned int` and to `unsigned long` get the label.
The functions are shared by the ports, and mcs51 was the only port tested with a wide literal.

## Related

Bug #3973 reports this output for a `const void *` object that is initialized with a narrow string
literal. Its test case also fails with the small model, because the object is `const` and the
compiler emits its value as data. The fix that its entry outlines was not implemented.
